headline: サンキュー is borrowed from English thank you.

meaning: to grow hazy, to be misty
headline: Kasumu is from Old Japanese and cognate with 霞める (kasumeru, “to blur, to obscure”) and かすか (kasuka, “faint, dim”).

sources.quote: From stem kasu-, cognate with its active counterpart 霞(かす)める (kasumeru, “to blur, to obscure”), adjective かすか (kasuka, “faint, dim”, and its classical form 幽(かすけ)し (kasukeshi)), adverb かすかす (kasukasu, “barely”), verb 掠(かす)める (kasumeru, “to rob; to sweep over”),, and verbs 擦(かす)る (kasuru, “to graze, to touch lightly”) and かすれる (kasureru, “to graze; to be blurred; to be hoarse”).
Cognate with 霞(かす)む (kasumu, “to grow hazy, to become blurry”) above.

examples.ja: 近くの物がかすんで見えます。

headline: Mashi is the continuative stem of the verb 増す (masu).

sources.quote: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 増(ま)す (masu).

examples.ja: 遅くともしないよりまし。
furigana: くともしないよりまし。

examples.ja: 天気は今日の方が少しはましだ。
examples.en: The weather is a shade better today.

meaning: to respect, to honor, to esteem, to prize
headline: Omonjiru is a shift from the verb 重んずる (omonzuru), as -uru verbs moved to the -iru pattern.

sources.quote: Shift from verb 重(おも)んずる (omonzuru), by natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

examples.ja: 彼は学校で重んじられた。
examples.en: He was made much of at school.

examples.ja: その子は両親を重んじた。
examples.en: That child thought much of his parents.

headline: ロープ is borrowed from English rope.

examples.en: Don't let go of the rope.

meaning: to swell (out), to be inflated, to bulge
headline: Fukureru is from Old Japanese 膨る (pukuru), and the source compares 袋 (fukuro, “bag”), from the way a bag is filled with items.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese 膨る (pukuru), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”), from Proto-Japonic *pukoru.

Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
Compare 膨らむ (fukuramu, “to swell, to get bigger”), 膨らます (fukuramasu, “to make swell, to fill up”), and 袋 (fukuro, “bag”), from the way a bag is filled with items.
First cited to the Man’yōshū, completed sometime after 759 CE.

examples.ja: たくさん食べたので腹が膨れた。
examples.en: I've had enough, so my stomach is full.

examples.ja: 彼女はそれで遊ぶことを拒んで、ただ座ってふくれていたのです。
examples.en: She refused to play with it, and just sat there looking angry.
furigana: ってふくれていたのです。

headline: Ware is from Old Japanese, the long form of 我 (wa) plus れ (-re, nominalizing suffix).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese, as the long form of 我 (wa) below.
Compound of 我 (wa, see below) + れ (-re, nominalizing suffix).
